title: Run the manual, account-bound OAuth compatibility check
statement: Against a real subscription and outside CI: run Pi's interactive `/login` with an isolated configuration directory and a sanitized environment; after it exits, construct a fresh `ModelRuntime` and `ModelRegistry` and record whether the chosen built-in model appears in `getAvailable()` and passes `hasConfiguredAuth()`; then remove or revoke the stored credential and record that the model becomes unavailable. Retain a sanitized single-instance evidence record — no token, header, credential-derived value, username or home path — and label it as manual and account-bound so it is never mistaken for a suite result.
notes: ⚠️ MANUAL AND OUTSIDE CI BY DECISION, not by omission. Automating it would require a real subscription credential in CI, which REQ-0024 forbids. ⚠️ DO NOT FABRICATE THE CREDENTIAL. Writing a canonical-shaped OAuth record into `auth.json` proves the shape round-trips and nothing about whether a subscription authenticates; the spike already did exactly that and the model stayed unavailable, which was a fact about provider composition rather than about OAuth. ⚠️ THE REVOCATION CONTROL IS THE HALF THAT CARRIES THE RESULT. Without it a model that was already available for an unrelated reason reads as a successful login. ⚠️ UNTIL THIS RUNS, no criterion and no section of the specification may state the OAuth route as verified — 'supported' is what the documentation may say.
